title: In-process message queue is unbounded — silent message loss when NNTP is down
description: Scenario: usenet-ipfs-reader NNTP endpoint goes down or is slow. Behavior: SMTP sessions keep accepting messages and enqueuing to MessageQueue (mpsc::unbounded_channel). Memory grows without bound. When queue consumer task eventually fails an NNTP POST, it logs warn\! and the message is dropped permanently — no dead-letter queue, no retry, no counter. Maintenance consequence: operators will file issues about 'messages disappearing during reader restarts'. Fix: bounded channel with backpressure (sender blocks or rejects) or persistent queue (SQLite). At minimum, add a monotonic drop counter.
